title: I Let the Ice-Hut Heater Hours Catch the Neighbor Who Camped My Auger

parts.text: I stepped into hut 12 at 5:03 a.m. and neighbor Bram was already using my numbered auger. The board said: ONE HUT. FOUR HOURS. AUGERS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-seven, club treasurer, holding a clipboard that listed our hut. Bram shrugged. "Neighbors keep the hole." I photographed the board, the booking, and his tip in my hole. Then I asked for the heater hours. At 5:11 the lake desk pinged why Bram's tip was in hut 12. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The lake desk can see Bram's tip in hut 12 during our four hours.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered auger in hut 12 — Part 1/2
social.description: Ice hut, a neighbor in my hole, a four-hour clock he posted. I logged the tip. Would you have asked for the heater hours?

parts.text: Bram called it pre-drilling until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the hut still. The auger went back to my numbered sleeve. Bram ran a slot of their own and told the next neighbor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: NEIGHBORS DO NOT KEEP THE HOLE. I keep our hut on a labeled tag. Bram brown-bags his tips. The hut finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Neighbors do not keep the hole — Part 2/2
social.description: Heater hours, numbered auger, and a second line on the board. Was pre-drilling ever our hut?
